title: Commercial Fusion Energy in 2026: Hard Milestones, Harder Funding

stats.label: ITER tokamak core now in place
stats.detail: Sixth of nine sector modules installed 29 July 2026, almost six months ahead of schedule.

stats.label: U.S. target for fusion deployment
stats.detail: DOE's June roadmap aims to catalyse early-stage plants; industry says funding is the X factor.

stats.label: Record fusion investment in 12 months
stats.detail: Worldwide in the year to July 2026; cumulative funding since 2021 reached $14.24 billion.

stats.label: U.S. fusion companies in the field
stats.detail: Most are developing tokamaks or stellarators; some pursue laser-based inertial confinement.

stats.label: Final ITER sector module target
stats.detail: Installation advanced from December 2027 to mid-2027 after faster assembly.

stats.label: Tritium half-life driving breeding need
stats.detail: Tritium is scarce; future reactors plan lithium breeding blankets to generate fuel.

quotes.text: The plan isn't the problem. We all agree on the plan. The X factor is the funding.
Private developers have not yet achieved 'net energy gain,' the point where a fusion reaction produces more energy than was used to start and sustain it.
With six modules now in place, we are demonstrating that this technical approach is delivering tangible results on the project's critical path.
ITER is primarily an exploratory science initiative and is not designed or intended to produce electricity.

takeaway: Fusion's 2030s deployment goal now hinges less on the physics milestone than on sustained funding and solving tritium breeding and neutron-resistant materials.
